newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin wants four leaders to agree main issues.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin wants four leaders to agree main issues.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Monday his prime minister, his top Kremlin aide and the heads of Russia's two houses of parliament should start meeting regularly to reach a consensus on important issues.

His proposal, made at a meeting with the lower house speaker Gennady Seleznyov, appeared intended to improve cooperation between the main branches of power and avoid confrontation as he prepares for heart surgery next month.

"We cannot at this time have people running off in different directions and everyone trying to solve problems on their own," the 65-year-old president said in brief television footage of the meeting at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow.
Yeltsin looked relatively well and spoke coherently.

His press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, said the four would be Seleznyov, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais and Yegor Stroyev, the speaker of the Federation Council upper chamber.
Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing that the four should meet regularly. He gave no schedule and did not say what powers they would have.
"In the current situation such meetings could become an effective mechanism to search for agreed solutions to the most important issues of the country's life," Yastrzhembsky said.

Yeltsin's proposal followed his sacking last week of security tsar Alexander Lebed, whom he accused of acting on his own and openly seeking to become president. Lebed's four months in the Kremlin were marred by intense politicial infighting.

Yastrzhembsky said there had been no changes to the proposed schedule for Yeltsin's heart operation, in which new veins will be grafted in to bypass blocked coronary arteries and improve the supply of blood to his heart.
"The preparations for the president's operation are continuing, there are no changes," Yastrzhembsky said.
A date for the operation has not been announced but one of Yeltsin's doctors said last week that it was expected to go ahead in the middle of November.
